comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, way/530531925 (Aspen Mountain, above the town of Aspen), one of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains, on its own map by the owner's rule of 2026-11-14 (one map per ski area unless the areas are connected by lift or trail): Aspen Highlands and Buttermilk, whose polygons reach into the box, are listed neighbours and left off. No lift or trail joins the four mountains; the resort links them by free buses (the 4-Mountain Connector on aspensnowmass.com/visit/getting-around; the Rubey Park bus station's 'free shuttle to all mountains' on this map), and each has its own ski area boundary and trail map. Split from the retired combined map aspen-snowmass: its twelve overrides that touch Aspen Mountain's features are carried here with their reasons (checked 2026-10-21 against the same map). Checked again on 2026-11-14, every named run and lift, against the resort's current sources: the 2025-26 trail map (2526aspenmountainwebsite.pdf, the edition aspensnowmass.com/four-mountains/trail-maps still links; its text layer gives the spellings, and it was rendered at four to twelve times its size to read the symbols) and the grooming report's trail list for Aspen Mountain (aspensnowmass.com's GroomingReport feed: 139 ski trails, each with its rating; the combined map's check had read the lists of Snowmass and Buttermilk only). The legend: More Difficult (blue square), Most Difficult (black diamond, a black line), Expert Only (two diamonds on a yellow line), Extreme Terrain (EX on a yellow line), OSM's intermediate, advanced, expert and extreme; no beginner terrain. OpenStreetMap is as the combined map's data of 2026-10-22 had it here (in the four mountains' window only the Elk Camp chair's line at Snowmass was edited since). Of the 142 named OSM runs, the map and the list agree with OSM after the carried overrides but for six. Upper Jim's, Expert Only on the map's Hero's view and expert in the list, becomes expert. Bell Meadow (a Most Difficult line on the map), the El Avalanchero and E=m(SKI)2 glades (black labels with no line or diamond, which do not tell Most Difficult from Expert Only) and Lud's Lane (a flat catwalk, unrated on the map) take the list's harder rating (expert, expert, expert and advanced), by the rule of 2026-10-22: where the resort's sources disagree, or only one of them rates a run, the harder of theirs and OSM's is kept. So Traynor Ridge stays extreme (OSM; advanced in the list, a black label on the map), and North Star and Pussyfoot stay advanced (black lines on the map, as in OSM; the list's upper Northstar and Pussyfoot Flats are blue). Names that differ from the list's only by a space, an abbreviation, punctuation or a piece's number stay, the map printing most of them as OSM has them (Star Walk, Powerline I and II, Gent's Ridge for the list's Gentleman's Ridge, 1 & 2 Leaf, Reds Run, E. 5th Ave and West 5th Ave). Hidden: the World Cup course's outline (America's Downhill). Lifts: OSM's six are the six the resort's snow report counts for 2026-27: the Silver Queen gondola, Ajax Express, F.I.S., Ruthie's, Hero's and Nell Bell, which the resort's Aspen Mountain page calls new this season, from Gondola Plaza to the top of Bell Mountain, where the 2025-26 map draws the Little Nell and Bell Mountain lifts; the 2025-26 map's Shadow Mountain lift is in neither OSM nor that count. OSM gaps against the map and the list (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Beattie Way, Tower 7 Road, Gent's Flats and Hero's Chutes #1 and #2 (OSM has the traverse to them).
